shared_elements: tall vertical stone monolith / pillar form
stacked vertical registers of figures, one above another
predatory animal head with bared teeth at the top
human or humanoid face with eyes and nose
bird-like creature with beak in profile (lower zone)
arms/limbs with elongated fingers rendered against the body
horizontal band of repeated small motifs across the upper part
justification: Both are tall stone uprights organised as a vertical stack of registers in which a toothy, snouted predator head crowns the composition above a human-featured element with arms and lower animal/bird forms, and both carry a horizontal band of repeated small motifs across the upper zone. The decisive difference is technique and mass: A is a bulky three-dimensional sculpture carved in the round with deeply modelled, protruding features, while B is a flat slab with shallow, linear low relief and a much more crowded, pictorial arrangement of separate creatures.
